nodes.name: Prepare Postgres table

parameters.query:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS demo_events (
  event_id   BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  run_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
  site       TEXT,
  status     TEXT,
  note       TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ
);

nodes.notes: Idempotent DDL: the demo owns its schema, no manual setup needed.

VALUES ('{{ $('Init run').first().json.run_id }}', 'MILANO_PLANT', 'received',
        'Ticket handed over to the maintenance crew')
RETURNING event_id, run_id, status;

=UPDATE demo_events
SET status = 'acknowledged', updated_at = NOW()
WHERE run_id = '{{ $('Init run').first().json.run_id }}'
RETURNING event_id, status, updated_at;

nodes.name: Read Postgres directly

parameters.query:
=SELECT event_id, run_id, site, status, note, created_at, updated_at
FROM demo_events
WHERE run_id = '{{ $('Init run').first().json.run_id }}'
ORDER BY event_id;

nodes.notes: Postgres is read directly with SQL: no Cortex layer in between.

nodes.name: AI Agent through Cortex

parameters.text:
=You are reporting on Snowflake memories for run {{ $('Init run').first().json.run_id }}.
Use your tools, never your own knowledge, and do all of the following:
1. Call ticket_stats and report how many open tickets each site has.
2. Call search_procedures asking what to do when the E5 packer sealing bar trips twice in one shift, and summarise the procedure in one sentence.
3. Call recent_events and report the status of the most recent Postgres event.
State which tool produced each answer. Be concise.

options.systemMessage: You are a reporting agent for a Snowflake demo. You have three tools, each backed by a different Snowflake memory: a standard table reached over the SQL API, a document corpus reached with Cortex Search, and a Snowflake Postgres database. Answer only with data returned by the tools, never from your own knowledge, and always say which tool produced each figure. If a tool fails, report the failure instead of guessing.

nodes.notes: Reasons across all three memories. The LLM is served by Snowflake Cortex.

parameters.content:
## 1. Standard table
Write with INSERT and UPDATE through the SQL API, then read back in natural language with Cortex Analyst.

Every Snowflake call goes through the private Cortex proxy: SPCS forbids PAT bearer tokens from inside a container.

## 2. Document corpus
Append a runbook chunk, wait out the one minute search lag, then retrieve it with Cortex Search.

The wait is honest: TARGET_LAG is how fresh the index is, and the demo writes and reads inside the same execution.

## 3. Snowflake Postgres
A dedicated BURST_S instance. The workflow creates its own table, writes, updates and reads it back with plain SQL: no Cortex layer in between.

## 4. One agent over all three memories
The LLM is served by Snowflake Cortex through the same private proxy, exposed as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. No data and no prompt leaves Snowflake.

The proxy collapses parallel tool calls: without that, Cortex rejects any agent turn with more than one tool call.
